{"redo_booking_notes":"🏝️ Cook Island Trip – Confirmation & Safety Info
We’re excited to have you joining us for a trip at Cook Island (Jungarra Ngarrian) — one of Australia’s top marine reserves!
Please read the key info below to ensure a smooth and safe day.
11. Gear Handling: You’ll carry your own gear from the trailer to the boat (approx. 50m).
Please handle all equipment with care.
After the trip:
Return all gear to the trailer at the jetty
Once back at the dive centre, rinse the gear you used in the designated wash area
Turn wetsuits right-side out before placing them in the rinse station
Thanks for helping us look after shared gear.
Surface Interval: After the first dive, change tanks immediately once safely back on the boat
Reassemble and secure your equipment without delay so you are fully prepared for the second dive
Once your gear is organised and ready, relax and enjoy your surface interval
Keep weight belts, masks, and fins neatly stored and clear of walkways and seating areas at all times.","redo_booking_highlights":"","redo_booking_what_to_bring":"9. What to Bring: Pack light — space on the boat is limited!
Only bring the essentials:
swimmer
towel,
sunscreen
water
light snack
Avoid large bags or bulky items.","redo_booking_what_not_to_bring":"","redo_booking_what_included":"","redo_booking_what_excluded":"","redo_booking_extras":"","redo_booking_meeting_point":"2. Meeting Point & Timing: Gold Coast Dive Centre
2/54–56 Paradise Ave, Miami QLD
Please arrive at the time shown on your booking
(e.g., for a 6:30 trip, check in by 6:30).
We can’t accommodate early arrivals, but there will be plenty of time to get ready once checked in.
3. Parking: Free on-street parking nearby.
Please allow extra time for parking, especially during busy periods or roadworks","redo_booking_check_in":"","redo_booking_before_arrival":"1. Sign Your Waiver: All participant must complete the digital waiver before arrival.
You'll find the link in your booking confirmation email.
Please complete it in advance to avoid delays at check-in.","redo_booking_departure_info":"","redo_booking_itinerary":"","redo_booking_duration_text":"","redo_booking_important_info":"7. Weather & Plan Changes: Cook Island is weather-dependent, and sometimes trips get cancelled due to conditions.
Weather is unpredictable and cancellations are beyond our control.
We appreciate your patience and understanding as we prioritise safety.","redo_booking_health_safety":"8. Seasickness & Remedies: Due to the location of Cook Island, seasickness can be an issue.
We recommend taking a seasickness remedy (e.g., Travacalm, Travalcalm HO, or Kwells) 30 minutes before boarding.
Bring extra remedies with you — Natural remedies (like ginger) are not as effective.
13. Best Practices & Dive Briefing: Giant stride entry off the Ocean Adventurer
Max depth: OW 18m, AOW 30m
No-decompression dives only
Max bottom time: 45 minutes
Surface interval: 30 minutes
Always dive in Buddy Teams and complete a pre-dive check
Lost Buddy Procedure: 1-minute search → ascend → inflate SMB → signal the boat
Air Guidelines:
100 bar = turn around
70 bar = begin ascent
50 bar = minimum surfacing pressure
Safety stop 3/5 minutes at 5 metres on all dives
Surface Hand Signals (When on the Surface): If communicating with the boat:
OK → Form a clear “OK” sign above your head\
Not OK → Raise one arm straight up above your head
Help / Distress → Wave one arm side to side above your head until assisted
Always stay with your buddy and deploy your SMB if required.
Emergency Recall: If you hear:
Continuous loud banging on the hull
Repeated engine revving
This indicates a full recall to the boat.
Stop immediately, stay with your buddy, and return directly to the vessel.
Exit procedure: Approach the boat and wait for crew instruction
Keep your mask and regulator in place until instructed otherwise
Hand up loose equipment if instructed
Remove weights and fins before boarding while holding the ladder
Board carefully using three points of contact
Once onboard:
Remove your regulator once stable on deck
Secure your mask either on your face or around your neck — do not carry it loosely
Store fins and weight belts neatly in the designated area
Keep all gear clear of walkways and seating areas
Avoid placing equipment on benches unless instructed","redo_booking_restrictions":"4. Proof of Certification: Certified divers must bring proof of certification (physical or digital), showing:
Your full name
Photo
Your certification level
The certifying agency
Logbooks are not accepted.
If you’re SSI certified and can’t find your card, contact us at least 24 hours in advance, and we’ll try to look it up.
5. Diving Ability, Confidence & Fitness: Cook Island is an open-ocean site. Conditions can vary and may include currents, swells, and winds.
Divers should be confident, fit and competent to dive in open-water conditions.
If unsure about your skills, we strongly recommend booking a private guide.
While group dives are guided, divers are expected to be self-sufficient, capable of managing their equipment and confident in their skills to avoid affecting the group.
The minimum certification level for regular dives is SSI Open Water Diver or equivalent; below this (e.g., SSI Scuba Diver) requires a private guide.
6. Recent Diving Experience: If you haven’t dived in 12+ months or more, you must complete the SSI Scuba Skills Update.
Divers with 250+ logged dives may be eligible to complete a Pool Check-Out Dive instead.
If it has been 4 years or more since your last dive, you will need to repeat the Open Water Diver course.
12. Diving Etiquette: Arrive on time and be ready
Be a good buddy, look out for each other
Be self-sufficient with your gear
Respect marine life and fellow divers.
Practice excellent buoyancy control
Follow the SSI Blue Oceans Philosophy: don’t touch, don’t take
Cook Island Marine Reserve Code of Conduct: Cook Island is a protected aquatic reserve. Help us protect it.
Look, don’t touch marine life, even shells
Keep your distance — Don’t chase or crowd animals
Stay 3+ metres from turtles and never block their path
No feeding or baiting marine life
Don’t rest or grab rocks or reef
Control your fins to avoid contact with reef or sediment
Maintain buoyancy and stay horizontal above the seabed
Secure all gear to prevent dragging
Avoid flash or prolonged light when photographing
Use reef-safe sunscreen or wear protection
Leave artefacts undisturbed
Remove floating litter if safe to do so
By completing your booking, you acknowledge that you’ve read and understood the safety guidelines and requirements outlined above.","redo_booking_special_requirements":"","redo_booking_accessibility":"","redo_booking_group_size":"","redo_booking_cancellation":"","redo_booking_disclaimers":"14. Any gear or items brought on the trip are at your own risk. We are not liable for loss, theft, or damage.
Please check your belongings before leaving. Unclaimed items will be disposed of after a week.
We do not provide storage.","redo_booking_pricing":"","redo_booking_faqs":"","redo_booking_contact":"","redo_booking_flags":"separator rules omitted

Surface Snorkeling Only:
Our snorkel trips are for surface snorkelling only.
We do not offer freediving or breath-hold diving.
Weight belts are not permitted.
Gear Handling:
You’ll carry your snorkel gear from the trailer to the boat (approx. 50m).
Please handle all equipment with care.
After the trip:
Return all gear to the trailer at the jetty
Once back at the dive centre, rinse the gear you used in the designated wash area
Turn wetsuits right-side out before placing them in the rinse station
Thanks for helping us look after shared gear.
Personal Items:
Gold Coast Dive Centre isn’t responsible for personal items.

Respond with OK or Not OK

Stay with your buddy

BOOKINGS - A DAY AT DIRK:
Full payment is required at time of booking
Bookings are essential
TOUR DETAILS - A DAY AT DIRK:
The Adventure boat departs from Denham Commercial Jetty at 08:30am sharp. Check in is 8:15am. Please have your booking confirmation ready at check in. A Day at Dirk Tour includes lunch, barista coffee or herbal tea, guided tour of shearing shed, a 2.5 hr Surf Point and Blowholes 4WD Tour, one Signature Island Gin & Tonic and the use of kayaks and SUP boards. Return transfer back to Denham at 4pm.
If you have specific dietary allergies, Island Life Adventures must be notified 48 hours prior to the commencement of the tour via email to info@islandlifeadventures.com.au
REFUNDS / CANCELLATIONS - GUEST:
For bookings cancelled less than 3 days prior to departure or no shows, there are strictly no refunds.
For bookings cancelled between 3 and 30 days prior to departure, Island Life Adventures Pty Ltd will refund 50% of the amounts paid.
For bookings cancelled more than 30 days prior to departure, Island Life Adventures Pty Ltd will refund amounts paid less the non-refundable 20% deposit.
Cancellation fees will be deducted from the credit card held on file.
For bookings whereby a guest has chosen to leave the tour after it has started, there are strictly no refunds.
All cancellations requests must be in writing to info@islandlifeadventures.com.au and the cancellation date is the date written notice is received by Island Life Adventures Pty Ltd.
REFUNDS / CANCELLATIONS – ISLAND LIFE ADVENTURES PTY LTD:
Island Life Adventures Pty Ltd reserve the right to vary or cancel any tour at any time due to weather conditions, road closures, breakdowns, insufficient numbers, or any reason deemed necessary to ensure the tour is completed safely. A minimum of 6 guests are required for tour to be confirmed.
In such instances of cancellation, Island Life Adventures Pty Ltd will email the customer with regards to a choice of:
A credit to be used towards another trip date of choice.
A full refund including deposit.
Please note that Island Life Adventures Pty Ltd is not liable for any additional costs guests may incur because of this, so ensure you are adequately covered with Travel Insurance.
For bookings where full payment has not been received at least 14 days prior to the tour, Island Life Adventures reserves the right to cancel the booking without notice and retain any deposit paid.
CUSTOMER RESPONSIBILITY:
The customer is to supply to Island Life Adventures Pty Ltd with a valid email address or Australian phone contact number, so that Island Life Adventures Pty Ltd can contact the customer in the event Island Life Adventures Pty Ltd cancels/postpones a tour for weather, or any other reason. In these instances, Island Life Adventures Pty Ltd will email the customer regarding options.
You agree that you have provided a valid email address and Australian phone contact. You agree to advise Island Life Adventures Pty Ltd of any specific dietary allergies 48 hours (min) prior to the commencement of tour.
Customers are to arrive and be ready for check in 15 mins (minimum) prior to tour, any no shows will result in ticket/s being voided – no exceptions.
Island Life Adventures Pty Ltd strongly recommends customers obtain full comprehensive travel insurance so they are adequately covered in the event of personal accidents or injury, medical expenses, emergency repatriation and personal liability.
LIABILITY AGREEMENT:

You agree to abide by agents or other operators that facilitate tours for Island Life Adventures Pty Ltd terms and conditions and indemnify them from any/all liability. You also agree that these terms & conditions are governed by Australian Law.
VESSELS:
100% Wild is the main vessel Island Life Adventures Pty Ltd utilises to conduct it’s tours however Island Life Adventures Pty Ltd can use any vessel at any time for any reason to conduct the tours. Island Life Adventures Pty Ltd can refuse entry to anyone deemed unfit by the Captain for whatever reason to protect the safety of the vessel and other customers.
AGES:
Adult: 17 years and older
Child: 3 – 16 years
Infant: 0 - 35 months
CONCESSION/PENSIONERS/SENIORS:
Senior and concession cards, including full time student concession cards should be presented at check in.
SUGGESTED PREPARATION FOR TOUR:
It is suggested you bring your booking confirmation (printed or on mobile phone), water bottle, warm jacket, hat, footwear, camera, sunscreen, bathers and towel. Please be sure to arrive a minimum of 20 minutes prior to departure. Check in commences 15 mins prior and gate is shut 5 mins prior to departure.
HEALTH:
If you have mobility or health concerns you must inform us when booking. Passengers must follow the directions of our staff & crew before, during and after the tour. If you are accompanied by children, you are responsible for their safety at all times.
If you have specific dietary allergies, Island Life Adventures Pty Ltd must be notified 48 hours prior to the commencement of the tour via email to info@islandlifeadventures.com.au
There is no disability access aboard the 100% Wild, at either departure point, Denham Commercial Jetty or at Homestead Bay, Dirk Hartog Island.

PHOTOGRAPHY:
Island Life Adventures Pty Ltd reserves the right to take photographs and video footage during the tour that may include passengers and to use these photographs and video images for the purpose of advertising and promoting our tours in all media in perpetuity and without payment to the passenger/s. Your ticket confirms you allow that Island Life Adventures Pty Ltd has the right to reproduce, copy or use all photography and video taken onboard it’s vessel/s regardless of person/s taking the photo/video. You agree that all photos taken by yourself cannot be used in promotional or advertising without Island Life Adventures Pty Ltd written consent.
TICKETING TRANSACTIONS:
All our prices are in Australian Dollars (AUD) and include GST (Goods and Services Tax). All credit card transactions are processed in Australian Dollars (AUD).
PRIVACY POLICY FOR ONLINE BOOKINGS:
Island Life Adventures Pty Ltd is dedicated to keeping your details private. Any information we collect in relation to you is kept strictly secured. We do not pass on, sell or swap any of your personal details with anyone. We use this information to identify your booking.

Our commercial Kitchens Hire facilities is available to other parties to hire and therefore cleanliness is vital for uninterrupted use of Perth Kitchen Hire. During its operation Perth Kitchen Hire insists that the kitchen is to be left according to the standards set out in the Cleanliness Standard Checklist, which is provided prior to your first hire session.
Thorough cleaning of the Kitchen and its equipment is required as part of your Lease Agreement. Should the kitchen be left in an unsatisfactory manner at the conclusion of a hire session an approved cleaner will be appointed by Perth Kitchen Hire at the Lessees expense. A cleaning fee of $60 will be deducted from your Security Bond, with no further notice. This is to ensure the Lessee is Handing over the Kitchen to the next customer in the highest standard of cleanliness, as specified in the Perth Kitchen Hire Cleanliness Standard Checklist document, you signed and agreed upon.
Failure to comply with Perth Kitchen Hire’s cleanliness standards may result in the refusal to hire out kitchens in the future as this can cause a negative flow on effect to subsequent hirer’s experience with Perth Kitchen Hire.
Opening and Closing Down: This will be arranged prior to your booking with one of our Team.
Set Up: Permission may be given by Perth Kitchen Hire for you to deliver equipment to the kitchen up to 24 hours prior to your rental period. This is merely a gesture of good faith to allow the ‘Lessee’ sufficient time to set up. Please note that this request may be refused in instances where the kitchen is already hired to another party, or the facility is at full capacity.
Equipment Usage: A list of equipment included in the Kitchen for hire includes and is limited to:
All main equipment within kitchen i.e. ovens, oven trays, cooktops, benches and sinks. This does not include items stored on shelves that are rented by other hire clients.
Use of fridge shelving allocated for food preps, only during hire period, unless hired and paid for the purposes of storage.
All kitchen utensils and equipment such as pots, pans, utensils and electrical goods are to be supplied by you the client. No equipment is to be left at the kitchens unless storage arrangements have been made.
Should damage occur that renders any item unusable it is expected that it will be replaced as new by the Lessee.
Foodstuffs: It is expected that hirers will provide all necessary foodstuffs for their requirements. Perth Kitchen Hire will not provide any foodstuffs. Any foodstuffs left by the Lessee in the Kitchen after the hire period (refrigerated or not) will become the property of Perth Kitchen Hire and will in all likeliness be disposed of, unless storage arrangements have been made.
Deliveries: Perth Kitchen Hire is not responsible for receiving or checking deliveries and will not take any responsibility for incorrect deliveries. Please ensure that you have a representative on hand to receive or return any goods.
Parking: Perth Kitchen Hire is situated in a business strata title and parking is restricted to a few designated bays only. Parking bay usage differs during business and non-business hours. Access to the building is via the large sliding door and you can park temporarily outside this door to load and unload your vehicle. The carpark at the rear of the strata must be used during your hire session.
Utilities: Perth Kitchen Hire provides usage of utilities – water, power, gas and toilets as part of this rental agreement. Should it be deemed that unnecessary or excessive usage of these utilities occurs, then Perth Kitchen Hire reserves the right to oncharge these costs to the Lessee.
Safety: Should possibly dangerous situations or behaviour by the Lessee occur during their hire session, Perth Kitchen Hire reserves the right to shut the kitchen and any operations down. Should this be, directly through the actions of the renter, then all monies are non-refundable.
Food Safety: It is the responsibility of the Lessee to ensure you are operating within the requirements of the relevant Food Legislation for both the structure and Food Safety practices. Monitoring Food Safety requirements are undertaken by the Department of Health WA in conjunction with Local Governments and will not form part of the Perth Kitchen Hire responsibilities. All Local Government Registrations/Notifications, regarding your Food Business, is the responsibility of the Lessee.
Availability: Please note that all bookings are subject to availability and Perth Kitchen Hire reserves the right to cancel a booking should the kitchen be unusable for any OHS reason.
Probation Period: All bookings over a month will be subject to a 1-month probation period, during which time either party can cancel the Rental Agreement with no penalty.
Public Liability & Workers Compensation: The Lessee is required to confirm the attained Certificate of Currency for Public Liability & Workers Compensation and provide a copy along with the completed Rental Agreement.

WHAT STRATEGIES DO YOU USE?:
Video Analysis: We use video analysis to improve your surfing technique and skill level. Our high performance coaches film your surfing session from the beach, then sit with you to go over your footage in detail and give you constructive feedback on your strengths and areas in need of improvement. You then get to go back out in the water to put the advice in to practice. You will be amazed at how the slightest tweak can make you look and feel like a whole new and improved surfer!
Surf Skate boards: No wave is ever the same and conditions are forever changing. Practice makes improvements and getting the feel of how your body should be balanced and positioned is really important to nailing those turns you have always dreamed of! Competition Practice: This is optional for those participants who are competition surfers. If requested, we can hold mock competitions and run through successful heat strategies to improve your confidence and technique to be ready for your next comp.
Strength and Mobility Training: Improve your strength, speed and power through proper technique and motivation during our gym sessions. We use gymnastic equipment like trampolines and padded mats.

What to expect:
You will be paddling on the beautiful Sydney Harbour.
There can be a lot of boat traffic so we can sometimes spend a few minutes waiting for Ferries.
This is an easy paddle of about an hour each way depending on conditions
Any questions? Call or text Sam 04 5188 7675.","redo_booking_highlights":"","redo_booking_what_to_bring":"What to bring: You should bring water and a change of clothes for after the paddle in case you get wet. It is rare for anyone to fall in but you can get damp from paddle splash. You can bring phones and Cameras but remember there is a risk as they don’t float and usually don’t work if dropped in water. For anything with a touch screen it is a good idea to have a small cloth to wipe drops from wet fingers off the screen as drops on the screen can be sensed as a finger touch and make use difficult. Anything you don’t want to get wet should be in a zip lock bag as a minimum. There is very little room in a Kayak so back packs are best left behind unless very small.
What to wear: Paddling is a water sport so expect to get splashed.
Your feet will get wet so water friendly footwear is strongly recommended.
The clothing Golden Rules - your kayak clothing should:
NO COTTON or DENIM - when they get wet, they do not dry and remain cold and heavy!
When wet, your clothing must stay warm and dry quickly!
The key concept to bear in mind is layering. Several thin garments will keep you just as warm as a single thicker one, and are much more versatile. Remember you’ll need to think about staying cool as much as staying warm, and you can always add or subtract layers.
A light Nylon Jacket will keep out wind and water. Fleeces are OK. Avoid heavy Jackets.","redo_booking_what_not_to_bring":"","redo_booking_what_included":"What is supplied: Sydney Kayak supplies the kayaks and kayaking equipment, Breakfast and Sunscreen.","redo_booking_what_excluded":"","redo_booking_extras":"","redo_booking_meeting_point":"Directions: Quibaree Park is on Lavender Street Lavender bay and can be accessed by car as well as being a short walk from North Sydney train station and Milsons point Ferry.

{"redo_booking_notes":"Please read these notes carefully before your Te Araroa Whanganui River Journey, as they contain important information about how this section of the trail operates.
During the River Journey:
This is a self-guided freedom hire canoe journey
Customers are responsible for managing their own safety while on the river
All personal gear and food supplies travel with you during the river section
A full safety briefing and paddling instruction session is provided before departure
All paddlers must wear the supplied lifejacket / PFD at all times while on the river
Arrival in Whanganui:
Pull the canoe into the designated grassed area in Whanganui
Leave all supplied equipment underneath the canoe as instructed
Continue your Te Araroa journey south
DOC Accommodation Bookings:
DOC huts and campsites must be booked separately by customers prior to departure.
We can provide:
Recommended itineraries
Suggested overnight stops
DOC booking information
Paddling distances
River maps and tide timetables
upon request.
Additional Costs:
Any additional shuttle, recovery, evacuation, or jet boat assistance required due to weather, fatigue, injury, or personal choice will be at the customer’s cost.","redo_booking_highlights":"","redo_booking_what_to_bring":"","redo_booking_what_not_to_bring":"","redo_booking_what_included":"","redo_booking_what_excluded":"","redo_booking_extras":"","redo_booking_meeting_point":"","redo_booking_check_in":"","redo_booking_before_arrival":"Before You Reach the River:

Once you arrive in Taumarunui, please contact Owhango Adventures via:
Email - info@owhangoadventures.co.nz
WhatsApp - +61408192429
Phone call - +64274567386
Text message - +64274567386
Please provide:
Your name
Group size
Approximate arrival dates
Estimated Whakahoro departure date
This allows us to coordinate your food storage, equipment, and river departure logistics.
Grocery Shopping & Food Storage:
Before continuing your Te Araroa walk south, complete your grocery shopping at New World Taumarunui for the Whanganui River section of your journey.
We will meet you at New World Taumarunui and collect your groceries directly from you.
Your supplies will then be securely stored at our Owhango base in:
Dry storage
Industrial chiller
Commercial freezer
depending on your requirements.
Free Camping at Owhango:
When passing through Owhango during your Te Araroa walk, hikers are welcome to camp free of charge at our Owhango base.
Facilities available include:
Showers
Toilets
Free WiFi
Lounge area
BBQ facilities
Microwave
Jug and toaster
Charging facilities
This provides a convenient place to rest, recharge devices, reorganize gear, and prepare for the next section of the trail.
Two River Departure Options:

Continue hiking from National Park / Waimarino to Whakahoro over the following days.
We will meet you at Whakahoro with:
Your groceries
Canoe
Paddling equipment
Dry barrels
River maps
At Whakahoro we will:
Conduct a full safety briefing
Assist with packing dry barrels
Explain river logistics and safety procedures
Provide river maps and tide information

Reorganize equipment
Prepare for the river section

{"redo_booking_notes":"Thank you for your booking, you will receive a seperate email advising pick up times for Kuranda and Daintree Rainforest, make own way to the Cairns Marina, Reef Fleet Terminal for the Great Barrier Reef Tour
Tour Highlights and Inclusions:
Cruise on board Evolution, a 35-metre luxury superyacht
5 hours of reef time at two exclusive Outer Reef sites
Unlimited snorkelling with equipment and flotation devices
Free lycra/sun suit hire
Spacious air-conditioned lounges and upper sun deck
Friendly, qualified crew and instructors
Inclusions:
BBQ lunch with fresh seafood, steak & salads (vegetarian & GF options available)
Complimentary glass of wine and snack on return
Reef levy (included in your package)
Not included:
Return Transfers - additional cost Cairns CBD ($24 per person) and Northern Beaches ($35)
Please contact us if you wish to include your hotel transfers
Diving Information:
Medical questionnaire required for all divers
Divers over 65 (or over 45 for PADI courses) must present a “Fit to Dive” medical certificate from their GP
Certain medical conditions or medications may prevent you from diving
Do not fly within 24 hours after your last dive
Certified divers must present a valid scuba certification card
Dietary Needs:
Please notify us of any special dietary requirements at least 48 hours before travel
After being picked up from your accommodation, travel to the Skyrail terminal for an amazing experience over Australia's World Heritage-listed Tropical Rainforest canopy descending into the forest at two stations, Red Peak and Barron Falls Guests can enjoy spectacular views from three lookouts at Barron Falls Station and learn more about the environment from ranger-guided tours at Red Peak Station.
Free time in Kuranda the village in the rainforest, with free time to explore the markets, shops, and animal attractions and speak with the locals.
Make own way back to your chosen accommodation
Look out for the “Billy Tea Safaris” vehicle.
Please be at your pick-up location 5-minutes before your pick-up time to ensure there are no delays.
Tour Inclusions:
1-hour Daintree River Cruise – spot crocodiles and birdlife
Morning tea – tea/coffee and biscuits
Cable ferry ride across the Daintree River
Scenic stop at Alexandra Lookout
Restaurant lunch at Cape Tribulation
Guided Elevated Boardwalk Tour – learn about rainforest ecology
Beach walk where the Rainforest meets the Reef
Tropical Fruit Ice Cream – Signature ice cream cup included
Other Information:
No paper vouchers needed – show confirmation on your phone
EFTPOS available for onboard purchases

{"redo_booking_notes":"Please read the SAFETY INFORMATION below. 👇 It is important for your safety and enjoyment.
Snorkelling in smooth waters: Wave Break Island is located within the Gold Coast Broad-water (inshore) and is therefore protected from ocean swells. It provides an ideal environment for beginners or for someone who enjoys calm and easygoing conditions.
Experienced snorkellers: Our snorkelling trips are primarily for surface snorkelling. We do not offer freediving or breath-hold diving and therefore snorkelling with a weight belt is not permitted.
Short notice plan updates may be sent: Wave Break Island is tide-dependent, therefore departure times vary depending on tide times. Although we can predict the tide flow, in-water activity involves other conditions that are beyond our control. If trips are cancelled due to weather, please understand this is for safety reasons (yours and ours) and is outside of our control. We know cancellations can be frustrating but please understand that the weather and sea conditions can be unpredictable and changeable and, are outside of our control. Please be kind and polite to our staff who are only working towards a safe operation. We have a zero-tolerance policy for rudeness or aggression towards our customers and team.
Boating: Boating on the Gold Coast is as good as it gets anywhere on the planet, and Wave Break Island is a huge area of smooth water protected from ocean swell, therefore there are no waves and it is very rare to suffer from seasickness. Sea sickness is also known as travel sickness, if you have motion sickness it is recommended to take a seasickness remedy 30 minutes before boarding. Travacalm original, Travalcalm HO and Kwells are 3 recommended types. Ginger/Natural remedy does not work.
Wave Break Island's environmentally conscious behaviour: In snorkelling, we often explore environments with biodiversity that is as exceptional as it is fragile. To limit our impact on the marine environment, there are a few simple rules we can all follow when snorkelling: no touching, collecting, damaging, feeding or moving marine life. Look and keep memories, but don’t touch and don’t chase or harass, please be mindful with your camera.
Snorkelling Etiquette:
Check your gear prior to entering the water.
Stay close to your Guide or Buddy Up with a partner.
Know your limits, take it one step at a time.
Respect Marine Life and Other Snorkelers.
Keep your fins up, especially when swimming over shallower formations.
Best Practices and Snorkel Briefing:
Please read this safety information. It is important for your safety and enjoyment.
All snorkelers are to be in “buddy pairs” to ensure the safety of each other. Children need to be under supervision at all times.
When snorkelling, the Boat must be visible at ALL TIMES. We need to see you to supervise you!
If the Boat Crew is signalling the OK signal, they are asking if you are OK. It requires an answer of “OK” or “Not OK” and “Help Me”.
Emergency recall to boat procedure (Continuous banging sound from boat or leader, continuous roaring Boat Engine).
Exit: remove fins before boarding, please leave your mask on. Hold on to the boat while taking your fins off.
Avoid the area around Engines, if they are running, do not come close without instruction from the Boat Crew.
Protect the Marine Park: No touch, No take.
If unsure of procedures, please ask Crew or staff.

{"redo_booking_notes":"Important info for your stay. Please pass this on to other members of your group.
The Timber Trail: The Timber Trail is 82km long and runs from Pureora in the north to Ongarue in the south. The Trail is graded easy-intermediate (grade 2-3) and runs along old bush tramlines and purpose-built single track. It is important to note the Timber Trail is in back country with no escape routes and limited cell reception, be prepared in case something goes wrong. A moderate level of fitness is required. The Timber Trail is very well signposted. There are kilometre markers every kilometre as well as directional markers whenever there is a fork in the track.
Bag Transfers: Your overnight bags go in a different van to you and your bike. Please ensure you have everything you need for your ride packed in a bag with you, and then your overnight gear packed in a separate bag to go direct to your accommodation. Please be considerate about how much gear you bring as space is often limited in the vans, especially on weekends and holidays.
Bike Hire: If you have booked to hire a bike, please make sure we have your height. Bike hire includes the bike, helmet and a bike repair kit. Note bikes do not have panniers, you need a backpack. Ensure you have signed the waiver for the bike hire terms & conditions above.","redo_booking_highlights":"","redo_booking_what_to_bring":"What to Bring for your Ride: You need to be dressed in appropriate gear for a full day of mountain biking in a back country area. The weather can be very variable so bring gear for both sunny warm weather and for freezing cold wet weather. You will need plenty of water and food for the day. Other items to consider are bike repair gear (spare tube, multitool, chain link and chain breaker, bike pump), sunscreen, PLB (can be hired from i-sites), first aid kit, camera, and change of clothes for after your trip.
Camp Epic Facilities & What to Bring: Camp Epic is self-catered so you'll need to bring your own food & drinks with you. We have cooking facilities so bring something yum to cook so you don't get food envy (don't bring freeze-dry meals). You are welcome to bring a chillybin. We do supply breakfast that you can help yourself to - tea, instant coffee, milo, uhf milk, bread, cereal (GF available), eggs, spreads. Our kitchen /dining area is fully equipped with all the cutlery, crockery & utensils needed. To cook we have gas cooktops, a bbq, and a grill tripod for over the firepit. There is a fridge for storing goods. Whilst we do have recycling bins we'd appreciate if empties were taken back out with you if possible due to our isolation from facilities.
If staying in our canvas tents, all your bedding and towels are provided. If you've booked a byo tent site you'll need to bring your own tent, bed, bedding, etc. Our ablutions block has flushing toilets & amazing hot showers, just bring your own toiletries. We have a fire pit to keep you toastie in the evening (marshmallows supplied). Please bring warm clothing and a beanie for the evening as it can get extremely cold at night all year round. In our kitchen/dining we have a small collection of books, playing cards & board games for your enjoyment. We run on solar power, so power is limited, but we do have facilities for charging ebikes & cellphones. Please be considerate of other guests and keep noise to a minimum after 10pm. Scuba Diving in smooth waters: Wave Break Island is located within the Gold Coast Broad-water (inshore) and is therefore protected from ocean swells. It provides an ideal environment for introductory diving or for someone who enjoys calm and easygoing conditions.
First Time Scuba Diving: Listen to your diving instructor above all else. No matter how experienced you might be, remember that your diving instructor is there to help you have a safe dive, first and foremost. If you're taking a scuba diving experience, then you should be certain to pay the utmost attention to what they are saying.
Short notice plan updates may be sent: Wave Break Island is tide-dependent, therefore departure times vary depending on tide times. Although we can predict the tide flow, in-water activity involves other conditions that are beyond our control. If trips are cancelled due to weather, please understand this is for safety reasons (yours and ours) and is outside of our control. We know cancellations can be frustrating but please understand that the weather and sea conditions can be unpredictable and changeable and, are outside of our control. Please be kind and polite to our staff who are only working towards a safe operation. We have a zero-tolerance policy for rudeness or aggression towards our customers and team.
Boating: Boating on the Gold Coast is as good as it gets anywhere on the planet, and Wave Break Island is a huge area of smooth water protected from ocean swell, therefore there are no waves and it is very rare to suffer from seasickness. Sea sickness is also known as travel sickness, if you have motion sickness it is recommended to take a seasickness remedy 30 minutes before boarding. Travacalm original, Travalcalm HO and Kwells are 3 recommended types. Ginger/Natural remedy does not work.
Wave Break Island's environmentally conscious behaviour: In scuba diving, we often explore environments with biodiversity that is as exceptional as it is fragile. To limit our impact on the marine environment, there are a few simple rules we can all follow when snorkelling: no touching, collecting, damaging, feeding or moving marine life. Look and keep memories, but don’t touch and don’t chase or harass, please be mindful with your camera.

{"redo_booking_notes":"The Experience: eFoilgc provides one on one instruction and the ride can be tailored to individual abilities.

You will be provided with a board that will best suit your needs.

One on one instruction and assistance: You will need to have enough upper body strength to be able to hang on to the board and transfer your weight back and forward. You will also need to be able to use the hand control to operate the board.

Your instructor will accompany you on a separate board. You will be provided with a headset for communication. Your instructor will be in radio contact with you at all times.

We can also offer escorted rides. For these rides, you are the passenger, and the board is controlled by the instructor.

You will get wet, and it can be cold at times, so if you have a wetsuit, please bring it along. If you do not have a wetsuit we can provide you with a rashie. You will be fitted with a life vest.

The entry point to the water changes depending on the tide. There is some sand to cross to get to the water’s edge. eFoilgc staff will help transfer you if needed.

Boat ramp at low tide: There is also a boat ramp nearby of a moderate gradient. The surface is grooved. The boat ramp is another option for entry to the water.

Rider with instructor alongside: The on shore assessment and instruction will take up to 25 minutes to complete. You will then be on the water for at least 25 minutes.

A rider having the board ‘foiling’: While you are on the water your instructor can take photos of you. You will be given the photos at no extra cost.

A video will also be taken and can be purchased at a separate cost.

Booking: If you have access requirements, we recommend you phone us to make your booking. We can discuss your needs during the call which will help us to understand how we can best support you to enjoy your eFoil experience.

Amenities: There is a public amenity block approximately 300 metres from the launching point. It includes a right hand unisex accessible toilet.

{"redo_booking_notes":"Hired RAW bikes will be pre-loaded onto the shuttle.
Self-guided ride from Arapuni back to Riverside Adventures base (approx. 14km; guideline about 1 hour per 10km). The Karapiro section of the Waikato River Trails is rated intermediate, featuring a mix of boardwalk, loose gravel surfaces, and some moderate inclines. Riders should have a reasonable level of fitness and confidence on uneven terrain.
Check out the official Waikato River Trail website: View karapiro (https://cdn.filestackcontent.com/0c7c6YLXS2lRwIuS8Oiz)
TWILIGHT KAYAK GLOW WORM TOUR:
Start times vary throughout the year due to sunset. You will be given a separate time that this portion of your Triventure starts
TWILIGHT KAYAK TOUR PORTION OF YOUR TRIVENTURE:
What's included:
Safety Briefing and paddling instruction.
Guide.
Splash pants and jackets.
PFD (personal Flotation Device).
Wetshoes provided.
Changing area and secure storage available.
Dry bag to store personal items in while kayaking.
Warm woollen socks (during Winter)
Plenty of parking onsite.
Itinerary:
Arrive & check-in– Arrive at our base and check in and get fitted with your gear. You will be sent a text message the day of your tour confirming the exact time of check in.
Safety briefing & setup – Meet your guides for a safety briefing and basic paddling instruction before heading out.
Paddle across Lake Karapiro – Begin with a gentle paddle along the lake edge, passing the submerged Horahora Dam while your guide shares local history.
Enter the Pokaiwhenua Stream – As the light fades, paddle into the sheltered canyon surrounded by native bush and birdlife. Continue upstream (approx. 1–1.15 hours / 1.5km)
Stretch & explore – There’s an opportunity to step out of your kayak, stretch your legs, and hear more about the history of the area before continuing. Stop for a 30-minute break.
Glow worm experience –Once darkness falls, retrace your path as you drift quietly back down the stream beneath a stunning display of glow worms lighting up the canyon walls.
Return to base – Continue your relaxed paddle back to base, taking in the peaceful night-time atmosphere.(approx. 45 minutes). covering around 3km in total.
What to bring:
Weather-appropriate clothing (layers recommended).
Camera for photos while upstream in daylight.
Special requirements:
Minimum age is 10 years; all children under 15 must be accompanied by a capable adult or guardian; ratio of 1 adult per child.
Please advise us in advance of any medical conditions, injuries, or mobility concerns.
A reasonable level of fitness is required.
All participants must follow safety instructions and wear provided safety equipment where required.
Evening temperatures drop during the return downstream.
Restrictions:
No jeans (they get very cold when wet)
Flash photography after dark is not allowed as it spoils viewing of glow worms for yourself and others. You can use cameras going upstream while its still light.
Minimum age is 10 years. All children must be accompanied by an adult or guardian, with a ratio of 1 adult per child.
If you do not meet this ratio (e.g. 1 adult with 2 children), please get in touch—an additional guide can be arranged to accompany a child at an extra cost.
Advertised weight limit for kayaking is 120kg.
NOTE: Riverside Adventures has zero alcohol & smoking policy on Glow Worm Tours.
Disclaimers:
Bookings are essential and minimum participant numbers apply.
This is a guided outdoor activity and operates in most weather conditions.
All participants must be able to understand and follow safety instructions delivered in English.
If participants are unable to understand English, they must arrange their own translator to accompany them.
Riverside Adventures Waikato reserves the right to refuse participation if safety instructions cannot be clearly understood.
Participants must be physically able to paddle.
If, after the initial paddle on Lake Karapiro, a participant is deemed unable to safely kayak, they will be guided back to base and no refund will be given.
Late arrivals may miss the safety briefing and may not be able to join the tour.

Gate closes 5 minutes prior to departure time","redo_booking_before_arrival":"","redo_booking_departure_info":"","redo_booking_itinerary":"","redo_booking_duration_text":"","redo_booking_important_info":"","redo_booking_health_safety":"Milford Sound Risk Disclosure:
Visitors to Milford Sound should be aware of various natural hazards when going to Milford Sound.
Aotearoa New Zealand:
Powerful natural forces have shaped Aotearoa New Zealand over millions of years. Earthquakes and volcanoes lifted these beautiful islands out of the Pacific Ocean. They have created the dramatic landscapes we enjoy today.
Natural hazards are part of life here. Around 20,000 earthquakes are recorded each year. Most are small and go unnoticed, but larger events can cause damage. Understanding the hazards and how to stay safe is an important part of planning your visit.
Piopiotahi Milford Sound:
Dramatic and ever-changing, Piopiotahi Milford Sound is one of the world’s most spectacular and special environments. Its steep, glacier-carved mountains and deep fiord have been shaped by powerful geological forces over millions of years.
The area is exposed to risk from a range of natural hazards. These can occur at any time, and some can happen without warning. Of all the hazards, large earthquakes, landslides and tsunamis pose the greatest risk to people at Piopiotahi Milford Sound.
It is extremely unlikely that one will happen during your visit, especially for a short stay. However, there is a risk and the longer you spend there, the higher it becomes. Once you are there, your safety options are limited and it is important you understand the risks, before you go.
Earthquakes at Piopiotahi Milford Sound:
Like the rest of Aotearoa New Zealand, small earthquakes occur regularly in Fiordland. We don’t feel them and they don’t bother us. These small movements are a normal part of how the land works and do not pose a risk to people.
Sometimes, earthquakes in or near Fiordland are felt at Piopiotahi Milford Sound. They might shake objects on a shelf or rattle a window, but they do not cause major impacts or disrupt your visit.
Occasionally, a stronger earthquake can trigger avalanches, rockfall or landslides. These can cause debris to fall onto roads, jetties and tracks, and may disrupt your travel plans if you happen to be nearby.
Large earthquakes are rare, and extremely unlikely to happen during a short visit. But they will happen again.
The Alpine Fault runs almost the entire length of the South Island and crosses the entrance to Piopiotahi Milford Sound. It can generate earthquakes of magnitude 8 or greater, occurring on average every 300 years. There is a 75% chance of this happening in the next 50 years (find out more at af8.org.nz) (https://af8.org.nz/). An earthquake of this size would almost certainly affect the narrow waterway and surrounding area.
What to do in an earthquake:
DROP, COVER and HOLD until shaking stops. Most injuries from earthquakes happen when you try and move during the shaking. The lower to the ground/floor you are, the less likely you are to be injured.
Follow staff instructions and/or move up and away from waterways (the fiord and rivers) as quickly as possible.
Landslides at Piopiotahi Milford Sound:
steep mountains around Piopiotahi Milford Sound are prone to rockfall and landslides. Earthquakes and severe weather can make the cliffs unstable, sending rock and debris down at speed.
Smaller rockfalls are common but often go unnoticed, unless you are nearby.
Bigger landslides do not happen often. The chance of one occurring during a short visit is extremely unlikely. However, they could cause a tsunami in the fiord and do pose a risk to life at Piopiotahi Milford Sound.
Large earthquakes are the most common trigger of big landslides in Fiordland. A large earthquake during your visit is extremely unlikely, especially for a short stay.
Be prepared for landslides:
Take extra supplies, food, water, first aid, clothes in your vehicle when travelling in remote areas, in case you get stuck – The road from Te Anau to Piopiotahi Milford Sound, is prone to avalanches, rockfall and landslides. It is monitored 24/7 by the Milford Road Alliance. However, if you get stuck, it will take time for help to reach you. Having extra supplies in your vehicle will make the wait time more comfortable.
If you see or hear a landslide entering the water, dust clouds, loud rumbling, or splashing. Follow staff instructions and/or move up and away from waterways (the fiord and rivers) as quickly as possible.
Tsunami at Piopiotahi Milford Sound:
Like all of Aotearoa New Zealand’s coastline, Piopiotahi Milford Sound is at risk of tsunami from multiple sources.
The most common threat comes from distant earthquakes in the Pacific Ocean. These ocean-source tsunamis take hours to reach our shores. Official warnings are issued in time for people to move to safety.
Less common, but of more concern, is the potential for a large landslide to fall into the fiord and trigger a tsunami.
Landslide-triggered tsunamis are rare. The chance of one occurring during your visit is extremely unlikely. However, they can create large waves and do pose a risk to life at Piopiotahi Milford Sound.
Be prepared for tsunamis:
Triggered by an earthquake – If you feel a LONG (1 minute or more) or STRONG (cannot stand up) earthquake, while at Piopiotahi Milford Sound, Get GONE. Move up and away from waterways (the fiord and rivers) as quickly as possible.
Triggered by a landslide – If you see or hear a landslide entering the water, dust clouds, loud rumbling, splashing or unusual water behavior, GET GONE. Move up and away from waterways (the fiord and rivers) as quickly as possible.
Plans and preparedness:
Piopiotahi Milford Sound has emergency response plans. These coordinate multiple agencies in a State or Emergency. The plans cover earthquakes, tsunami, landslides, avalanches, flooding, severe weather and other emergencies.
All tourism operators maintain their own emergency procedures. These integrate with the wider response in a State of Emergency.
If a large landslide triggers a tsunami, there will be no warning. Emergency support will take time to arrive. Visitors and workers should be aware of the risk to life and prepared to move up and away from waterways (the fiord and rivers) as quickly as possible.
For more detailed information, please visit Emergency Management Southland (https://civildefencesouthland.govt.nz/piopiotahi-milford-sound) or AF8 (https://af8.org.nz/).

For enquiries about your reservation, please contact the RealNZ team on contact@realnz.com (mailto:contact@realnz.com) or 0800 65 65 01 (tel:08006565010). For transport enquiries within 24 hours of your departure, please contact Altitude Tours on 03 441 4788 (tel:0344147880).

Natural hazards are part of life here. Around 20,000 earthquakes are recorded each year. Most are small and go unnoticed, but larger events can cause damage. Understanding the hazards and how to stay safe is an important part of planning your visit.

Piopiotahi Milford Sound: Dramatic and ever-changing, Piopiotahi Milford Sound is one of the world’s most spectacular and special environments. Its steep, glacier-carved mountains and deep fiord have been shaped by powerful geological forces over millions of years.
The area is exposed to risk from a range of natural hazards. These can occur at any time, and some can happen without warning. Of all the hazards, large earthquakes, landslides and tsunamis pose the greatest risk to people at Piopiotahi Milford Sound.
It is extremely unlikely that one will happen during your visit, especially for a short stay. However, there is a risk and the longer you spend there, the higher it becomes. Once you are there, your safety options are limited and it is important you understand the risks, before you go.

Earthquakes at Piopiotahi Milford Sound: Like the rest of Aotearoa New Zealand, small earthquakes occur regularly in Fiordland. We don’t feel them and they don’t bother us. These small movements are a normal part of how the land works and do not pose a risk to people.
Sometimes, earthquakes in or near Fiordland are felt at Piopiotahi Milford Sound. They might shake objects on a shelf or rattle a window, but they do not cause major impacts or disrupt your visit.
Occasionally, a stronger earthquake can trigger avalanches, rockfall or landslides. These can cause debris to fall onto roads, jetties and tracks, and may disrupt your travel plans if you happen to be nearby.
Large earthquakes are rare, and extremely unlikely to happen during a short visit. But they will happen again.
The Alpine Fault runs almost the entire length of the South Island and crosses the entrance to Piopiotahi Milford Sound. It can generate earthquakes of magnitude 8 or greater, occurring on average every 300 years. There is a 75% chance of this happening in the next 50 years (find out more at af8.org.nz (https://af8.org.nz/)). An earthquake of this size would almost certainly affect the narrow waterway and surrounding area.

What to do in an earthquake: DROP, COVER and HOLD until shaking stops. Most injuries from earthquakes happen when you try and move during the shaking. The lower to the ground/floor you are, the less likely you are to be injured.
Follow staff instructions and/or move up and away from waterways (the fiord and rivers) as quickly as possible.

Landslides at Piopiotahi Milford Sound: steep mountains around Piopiotahi Milford Sound are prone to rockfall and landslides. Earthquakes and severe weather can make the cliffs unstable, sending rock and debris down at speed.
Smaller rockfalls are common but often go unnoticed, unless you are nearby.
Bigger landslides do not happen often. The chance of one occurring during a short visit is extremely unlikely. However, they could cause a tsunami in the fiord and do pose a risk to life at Piopiotahi Milford Sound.
Large earthquakes are the most common trigger of big landslides in Fiordland. A large earthquake during your visit is extremely unlikely, especially for a short stay.

Be prepared for landslides: Take extra supplies, food, water, first aid, clothes in your vehicle when travelling in remote areas, in case you get stuck – The road from Te Anau to Piopiotahi Milford Sound, is prone to avalanches, rockfall and landslides. It is monitored 24/7 by the Milford Road Alliance. However, if you get stuck, it will take time for help to reach you. Having extra supplies in your vehicle will make the wait time more comfortable.
If you see or hear a landslide entering the water, dust clouds, loud rumbling, or splashing. Follow staff instructions and/or move up and away from waterways (the fiord and rivers) as quickly as possible.

Tsunami at Piopiotahi Milford Sound: Like all of Aotearoa New Zealand’s coastline, Piopiotahi Milford Sound is at risk of tsunami from multiple sources.
The most common threat comes from distant earthquakes in the Pacific Ocean. These ocean-source tsunamis take hours to reach our shores. Official warnings are issued in time for people to move to safety.
Less common, but of more concern, is the potential for a large landslide to fall into the fiord and trigger a tsunami.
Landslide-triggered tsunamis are rare. The chance of one occurring during your visit is extremely unlikely. However, they can create large waves and do pose a risk to life at Piopiotahi Milford Sound.

Be prepared for tsunamis: Triggered by an earthquake – If you feel a LONG (1 minute or more) or STRONG (cannot stand up) earthquake, while at Piopiotahi Milford Sound, Get GONE. Move up and away from waterways (the fiord and rivers) as quickly as possible.
Triggered by a landslide – If you see or hear a landslide entering the water, dust clouds, loud rumbling, splashing or unusual water behavior, GET GONE. Move up and away from waterways (the fiord and rivers) as quickly as possible.

Plans and preparedness: Piopiotahi Milford Sound has emergency response plans. These coordinate multiple agencies in a State or Emergency. The plans cover earthquakes, tsunami, landslides, avalanches, flooding, severe weather and other emergencies.
All tourism operators maintain their own emergency procedures. These integrate with the wider response in a State of Emergency.
If a large landslide triggers a tsunami, there will be no warning. Emergency support will take time to arrive. Visitors and workers should be aware of the risk to life and prepared to move up and away from waterways (the fiord and rivers) as quickly as possible.

LOCKING THE ITINERARY IN!:
Generally speaking, we have already spoken to you/the customer via email or text and have sent some prices and options to you. If you have mentioned exactly which option you wanted in your booking form that you just completed then we are immediately booking in all of the venues that we've discussed via email/text and you don't need to do anything in that regard. If, however you want changes/amendments to what we have spoken about, or if we hadn't fully agreed on an itinerary just yet, then please let us know ASAP as we need to get things locked in as soon as we can!

If we haven't spoken at all and you've booked this on your own based on what you've read on the website, then we will be reaching out to you shortly to get a gauge on what our exact itinerary and prices will be. Note: Prices on our website are more of an indicative price if the group is 11 or more people. If you have booked this without speaking to us and only have 2-8 people, the prices will be much more (almost double) than what you've probably read, so please contact us now so we can get on the same page and send some options to you :)

We don't require full payment until 3 DAYS BEFORE THE TOUR. So between then and now its your job to collect everyones payments and update us on numbers. We recommend you do this sooner than later. In our experience if you give people a chance to flake, they probably will! People will say "Yeah, I'm Keen, sign me up" , but then ask them to pay and they go silent...So thats why we say get started ASAP, even if its weeks away. This will filter out the flakey ones and give us a better idea on numbers early. Please don't consider anyone 'confirmed' unless they've ACTUALLY paid you.
This is important because often we have explained in our original quote that the 'price per person' will change based on how many people you have.

For example, if you were optimistic with numbers thinking you'd have 20 people, and our quote said $160 for 16-24 people, but $180 for 12-15 people, and then unfortunately a few drop out, then if you end up with 14 people, we will then expect 14 people paying 180$ basically meaning you are needing to ask for more money from everyone that is coming,....in this example....
So for that reason if you are unsure of how many people will come, we would recommend asking people for the higher amount so that you are best prepared for any drop in numbers.

DO YOU HAVE AN ESKY/COOLER ON THE BUS? A: We built our tours around having a fun and boozy day out and we always keep that at the forefront of our tours. We want you to have a fun time. And we also acknowledge that some feel wine tastings are not generous enough to really feel tipsy. We have a bit of a common sense approach to our tours. Where we feel, we will always put an extra bottle or two on the table if we feel the group needs it. We want you you to feel like you are getting your moneys worth. You will generally get 6-7 standard drinks in a space of 4-5 hours and also have the ability buy as much drink as you want on the day. We aim to be the most generous winery tour company in Melbourne. We believe most wine tours are operating in a very sleezy and lazy way, but taking your money and finding ways to give you as little alcohol as possible. We believe that if we give you lots of wine throughout the day, that you'll want to tell your friends about us and it keeps our business alive.
Because we are so generous, we really need to take your alcohol consumption seriously.
We NO LONGER ALLOW anyone to bring any drinks on our vehicles whatsoever. Unfortunately this is something that is policed quite heavily these days, and where we were once pretty lenient, we are no longer. There has been a few drivers in our industry who got caught allowing drinking on the buses and the driver themselves were the one that was punished. They lost their license as a result. This emphasises that the risk is all on your driver. In an ideal world we could pass the punishment onto you and the people drinking, but that simply does not happen. It's the driver. Stupid, I know, but those are the rules. And it has scared the entire industry. If you are drinking, you don't get in trouble, the driver does!
The simple fact is that it is illegal to drink any alcoholic drinks on any heavy vehicle. Every single wine tour is TECHNICALLY breaking the law when allowing drinking on the bus.
So for that reason we DO NOT ALLOW ALCOHOL ON OUR BUSES. We leave it to the day to apply some discretion, but we do not want anyone bringing drinks on the bus to start the day.
Please do not tell people they can bring drinks, and on that, tell them to NOT bring drinks.
PLEASE CALL ME IF THIS IS AN ISSUE FOR YOU.

We DO NOT provide coolers/eskys on our buses. You'll need to bring your own.

Description of image (https://cdn.filestackcontent.com/sJXa6f8NTPOmo5AMvkxT)","redo_booking_health_safety":"","redo_booking_restrictions":"","redo_booking_special_requirements":"","redo_booking_accessibility":"","redo_booking_group_size":"","redo_booking_cancellation":"CANCELLATION POLICY:
CANCELLING YOUR TRIP PRIOR TO DAY OF DEPARTURE:
Payment is required in full upon booking your charter. You may cancel or re‐book for another day ONE WEEK PRIOR to the day of your charter without any loss of your monies paid. Should you make a cancellation within one week of departure, for any reason, you will not receive a refund.
PRIOR TO DEPARTURE:
If the skipper calls the charter off due to bad weather you will have the option of the\ next day fishing if possible or if this is not possible a refund of monies paid for your fishing.

If you are out fishing and the skipper calls the charter off within 2 hours of your charter, you have the same option of a return trip or refund. If you are out to sea for 2 hours or more then there is no refund or return trip given.

If the skipper has doubts about the weather and advises not to go but you wish to go anyway there will be no refunds. If you call a charter off and wish to come in early there will be no refunds.
AT SEA:
If you have been at sea for under two hours and the skipper calls the charter off due to bad weather you will have the option of the next day fishing if possible or if this is not possible a refund of monies paid for your fishing.

If you have been at sea for more than two hours and either the skipper or all of the passengers call the charter off there will be no refunds.
SEA SICKNESS:
If you call a charter off because of sea sickness there will be no refunds.

For combined charters where sea sickness occurs, the charter must continue.

We highly recommend that you seek medical advice and obtain sea sick medication if you think you may suffer from sea sickness. The skipper is unable to provide you with any medication.

Returning a passenger to shore due to sea sickness will only occur if the skipper deems it necessary. If on combined charters some members are sick and some are not and the remainder of the passengers wish to continue with the charter, the skipper may return passengers to shore and then go back out to complete the charter. Should this option be taken the passengers wishing to return to shore will need to pay additional funds to cover the cost of petrol. The cost of such a return journey will depend on the estimated fuel usage and the amount will be told to the passengers before the return journey. Minimum cost $80.","redo_booking_disclaimers":"","redo_booking_pricing":"","redo_booking_faqs":"","redo_booking_contact":"","redo_booking_flags":"branding lines omitted: M.V. {"redo_booking_notes":"Additional Information:
Scheduling: In general camps are 3 days long 9.30-3pm with early morning drop off at 8.30 onwards and late afternoon pickup until 5pm. Your order will show the start day/time for the first day of the camp.
Sign-in and out: Please escort your child/children to the sign in desk at the back of Manly Sailing office (end of East Esplanade path) to complete the sign in process. Please let staff know if you would like your child to make their own way home and sign the appropriate permission slip or email us before hand.
Waiver: Each participant will be required to complete a waiver before participating in a course / experience. This can be done online (https://waiver.smartwaiver.com/w/5d8b0b333d047/web/) or at the office.
Location: Dinghy lessons will start from Manly Sailing. Our office is located on the wharf level underneath Many Yacht Club. When in Manly, facing the Manly Ferry Wharf, turn left and follow the path around past East Esplanade beach until it ends. A short 10 minute walk.
Food: Please bring recess, lunch and a water bottle (required) to keep them hydrated and full of energy to get through the day. We may stop for lunch at different beaches so please ensure they have their food and water ready to go in the morning.
Footwear: Old trainers or wetsuit booties to provide protection from sharp objects. Crocs and Thongs are not permitted (required) as they cannot be securely fastened to feet. Anyone arriving without secure footwear will not be permitted on the boats or the wharf.
Hat: A secure hat that can be tied on is recommended.
Shorts: Shorts over a wetsuit are essential as sailing involves sliding around on the boat quite a bit. If you have a wetsuit it is a good idea to bring it.
T-Shirt: A long sleeve rash vest must be worn (required) for sun protection and to prevent a rash caused by the PFD. Rash vests can be purchased from our office upon arrival.
Warm Top: such as an old polar fleece, or a light wind jacket is advised to add that extra layer if it’s chilly.
PFD (Personal Floatation Device): we supply PFD’s for all students. Students may use their own but we reserve the right to inspect them and if necessary insist that one of ours is worn. Anyone declining to wear their PFD will not be allowed to participate.
Sun cream: Participants should bring their own sun cream, preferably Zinc or at least factor 30 or above. Sun cream should be applied at home before attending and during camps our staff will supervise reapplication of sun cream at the lunchtime break. If your child has allergies to any sunscreens please ensure they have a suitable one packed.
Towel: Participants will get wet during the session so a dry towel for afterwards is essential.
Secure gear bag: is required to store all clothes and gear. We will do our best to make sure students gear is secure but we do not have lock up facilities so please don’t bring valuables. Gear should be labelled clearly to mix-ups / lost property. We will store lost property for a maximum of two weeks following an event.
Dry clothes: Participants will get wet during the session so a set of dry clothes for afterwards is advised. An old shopping bag is recommended to carry wet gear in is recommended.
Refunds and changes: Please see terms and conditions
